asks: The Grande Prairie County reeve asks the commission to weigh more than population for northern and rural ridings and to recommend that the legislature revisit the plus-or-minus 25 per cent rule.

note: Presenter mentions Slave Lake only for its resource revenue while arguing new seats should go to the north; Lesser Slave Lake riding was raised by a commissioner, not the presenter. Airdrie named only by a commissioner.

asks: Asks that Lesser Slave Lake be kept as it is, as a section 15(2) special division, with any added population taken from the east.

quote: I’m making a submission to the commission today in support of leaving the existing boundaries of the Lesser Slave Lake electoral division where they’re at.
page: PDF pp. 542-550 (before first EB label; EB-378/379)
note: Also: 'the Lesser Slave Lake constituency should be considered one of the special areas and afforded the exemption'. Argues against splitting it among neighbouring ridings (round 1 idea, not the interim K2 plan, so rejects left blank). If population must be added, suggests going further east.

asks: Suggests bringing the Flatbush area of the MD of Lesser Slave River back into Lesser Slave Lake to add population, and points to an uncounted shadow population.

quote: That may make some sense to bring them back into the fold of this constituency.
note: Answer to a commissioner's question on where to add population to keep Lesser Slave Lake; presenter is the Lesser Slave Lake UCP association president appearing with Vanderwell. Implies keeping the riding, enlarged with the Flatbush region.

asks: Asks that the east edge of West Yellowhead follow the Yellowhead County boundary (or Highway 751) so the county's east end is not split from the rest.
Asks for ridings aligned two-per-federal-riding, a north-south mountain riding for the West Yellowhead area, voter parity within 25 per cent, and team-based MLAs.

note: Asked by a commissioner whether a north-south mountain riding should take in Nordegg or go as far as Rocky, says 'I think it still fits'; tentative, no request about the Rimbey-Rocky Mountain House-Sundre riding itself.

Floats a north-south Rockies riding (Hinton/Jasper toward Lake Louise and Banff), saying 'You could include Rocky Mountain House or Edson. It depends.' Too tentative to code as a want (rule 17); closest would be B9.

asks: A Red Deer-South resident asks that rural and city areas not be mixed in one riding.

note: Says 'I wouldn't want to mix the two. I don't want to water down the concerns of rural areas versus the city' as a general principle (HYBRID-GENERAL G-CON); not tied explicitly to Red Deer, though she identifies as Red Deer-South. Rule 17: no want.
Asks about Red Deer's population growth only.

asks: A Rimbey-Rocky Mountain House-Sundre resident worries that enlarging rural ridings will hurt representation and says the riding's name suits it.

note: Says the name 'suits the riding'; concern about larger ridings, but no explicit request to keep it.
Comments on growth in Red Deer-North versus Red Deer-South only.

asks: The MLA for Cypress-Medicine Hat asks that the boundaries of Cypress-Medicine Hat and Brooks-Medicine Hat not be changed.

note: Named only as a comparison: Medicine Hat has more representation per capita than Red Deer, Lethbridge, Airdrie, Grande Prairie (rule 6).
Named only as a comparison (rule 6).
Named only as a comparison (rule 6).

asks: A Calgary-East resident asks that Calgary-East stay within Calgary's city limits and not be joined with Chestermere or rural areas, and that a seat be added in north Calgary.

quote: The other thing to me and, I think, to a lot of my colleagues that’s a concern is this idea of coupling us up specifically with Chestermere, which is a very, very different community
note: Also (PDF pp. 588-589): 'Its boundaries need to be aligned with Calgary's municipal boundaries and should not include parts of neighbouring rural communities.' Rejects joining Chestermere with Calgary-East; says nothing of what Chestermere should be with, so no want. Allows a 'Chestermere-East kind of thing' might come at a future review.

asks: Former Lethbridge mayor asks that Lethbridge not be split into four hybrid ridings and keep MLAs who represent the city alone.

quote: I’m here today because I heard that there might be a proposal to split up representation in Lethbridge into four hybrid ridings, basically partially rural and partially urban, and I’d like to speak against that proposal.
note: Want from: 'Lethbridge deserves what Calgary and Edmonton already have, and that is MLAs that are focused on fully understanding the needs of an urban centre' (PDF p. 591) and 'I don't see any advantage ... to having blended hybrid MLAs representing the city' (EB-404).
Named only as another mid-size city denied transit funding (rule 6).

asks: The City of Airdrie asks for new boundaries giving Airdrie two Airdrie-focused ridings sized for its growth, some including Crossfield and nearby rural areas, instead of the oversized Airdrie-Cochrane and Airdrie-East.

quote: Our proposals create community-focused ridings that reflect natural boundaries, travel patterns, and shared interests. The inclusion of Crossfield and surrounding rural areas in specific scenarios strengthens regional cohesion
note: Joint presentation with Megan Stewart (HANSARD-R1-T27-005), who described the three scenarios: two Airdrie-centred ridings split north-south or east-west, some with Crossfield and rural polls, south riding to Calgary city limits. Rejection from: 'I think it has been difficult for the MLA for Airdrie-Cochrane to effectively represent both communities' (EB-407). Says a one-urban-plus-one-hybrid design was tried and dropped because the urban seat would outgrow the limit.

quote: I think it has been difficult for the MLA for Airdrie-Cochrane to effectively represent both communities. Although we’re similar in terms of the infrastructure that’s required to support growth, our communities are significantly different from one another.
note: Answer to a commissioner's question on Cochrane in the riding. The Cochrane want (a dedicated Cochrane division with Bearspaw) is stated by Stewart in HANSARD-R1-T27-005; Esau's own words give only the rejection.

quote: The inclusion of Crossfield and surrounding rural areas in specific scenarios strengthens regional cohesion while facilitating beneficial adjustments to neighbouring electoral divisions.
note: Crossfield placed with Airdrie in some scenarios ('Crossfield belongs with Airdrie' maps to O2 per codebook). Only some scenarios include it; says nothing about Mountain View County or Sundre.

asks: The City of Airdrie presents three scenarios for two Airdrie-centred ridings, some with Crossfield and nearby rural polls, and supports a dedicated Cochrane riding with Bearspaw.

quote: In the rural areas, in addition to our own city boundaries of Airdrie and the town of Crossfield, our proposed scenarios could incorporate some rural voting stations in the areas surrounding Airdrie.
note: Scenarios: north-south split on Yankee Valley Boulevard with Crossfield in the north riding; east-west split on the CPKC line with and without Crossfield; south riding to Calgary city limits. Two Airdrie-centred ridings with nearby Rocky View and no part of Calgary: A1 in kind, though Crossfield goes with the north/west riding, not specifically the east one.

quote: we would support the creation of a dedicated Cochrane electoral division that would include the Bearspaw area, which would have strong community ties to Cochrane.
note: Same request as the city's written submission (codebook example 5).

quote: You notice that several of our proposed scenarios include the town of Crossfield within our proposed electoral boundaries.
note: Crossfield with Airdrie maps to O2. Also suggests moving Bowden into Olds-Didsbury-Three Hills; says nothing of Sundre or Irricana/Beiseker.

asks: A Lethbridge-West resident asks that Lethbridge keep its two city-only ridings and not be divided into four rural-urban ridings.

quote: This model works for Lethbridge, and I would respectfully ask that you please don’t try to fix what isn’t broken.
note: Rejection: 'dividing a city of 111,000 people that hasn't even adopted a municipal ward system into four quarters would make no sense at all.' Reacting to the four-riding proposal presented at the May 29 hearing; supports keeping Lethbridge-West and Lethbridge-East consistent with municipal boundaries.

asks: The MLA for Calgary-Acadia describes her riding's growth and asks that the two new seats go to Calgary and Edmonton.
A Lethbridge-East resident asks that Lethbridge's ridings stay within the city's own boundaries, with no hybrid district.

quote: I submit that Lethbridge needs to have its ridings within its own boundaries.
note: Rejection of any hybrid for the city: 'If a hybrid district were to be implemented, it could place these groups in a situation where they may never see like-minded people running or winning a seat' (EB-411); not aimed at the four-way plan in particular, so L3 included. St. Albert at the end of the record is a commissioner speaking to the next presenter.
